transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-09-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Location: Zoom - Fireflies auto-record
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Khalil (SE), Lina (CS), Priya (Juno CTO), Chris (ML), Mark (SRE), Devon (Security), Ava (Procurement)

Summary (auto-generated, edited):
Quick POC scoping to pick deployment mode and define success criteria: hosted vs dedicated vs private. Discussed workload sizing, bench targets (latency/throughput), data residency / compliance constraints, timeline and next actions. Customer leans toward hosted for speed but has strict data residency & KMS needs that could push to dedicated or private.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh -- we'll run through goals for the pilot and then Khalil will go over the test harness and what we need for sizing.
[00:18] Priya: thanks, Maya. high level - we want a 4-week POC to validate latency and cost against our call center summarization workload. main non-negotiable: logs with any PII scrubbed and customer-managed keys for model context.
[00:34] Maya: understood. that pushes a little bit toward dedicated/private but let's talk tradeoffs. can you give us some numbers on expected qps, avg tokens?
[00:47] Chris: sure — baseline is ~150 qps average, peaks to 650 qps during morning shift; typical prompt + response ~600 tokens combined, but 90% are <360 tokens. concurrency peaks are around 80 simultaneous requests.
[01:10] Khalil: ok that helps. rough calc: for 150 qps steady-state with 600 tokens avg, that's ~540k tokens per minute, 32M tokens per hour, which is — uh i might be off a hair — but it'll definitely shape whether hosted shared capacity can meet latency P95 targets.
[01:34] Mark: our latency SLO is P95 < 120ms for single-turn summary calls; we understand that for longer sequences that might be higher but 120ms is the bar for user-facing experiences.
[01:46] Khalil: noted. that P95 is tight at 600 token responses; most infra will struggle in hosted shared mode unless you pick a small-ish model or accept higher latency.
[01:59] Priya: can you explain 'small-ish model' vs model parallelism? we plan to use a tuned open model — roughly Llama-3-13B quantized or similar.
[02:12] Khalil: 13B quantized is a good middle ground. on A100 class hardware or equivalent, with continuous batching and KV cache you'd likely hit ~80-200ms depending on batching and seq len. to reach sub-120ms P95 consistently at peak, you'd look at dedicated GPU capacity (reserved), or dedicating endpoints with pinned kernels and aggressive batching control.
[02:41] Maya: decision criteria we typically recommend: cost sensitivity (hosted is cheapest up-front), determinism & throughput needs (dedicated), and compliance/data residency/KMS (private or dedicated with VPC). Also time-to-value — hosted can onboard in days.
[03:01] Devon: on KMS and data residency — we must ensure model context storage is customer-managed KMS and logs don't leave EU. we have contractual residency requirements.
[03:12] Maya: that makes private or dedicated with VPC egress controls more likely. but we can set up a hybrid POC: start hosted for functionality + rapid integration, then run performance bench on dedicated nodes as second phase.
[03:27] Chris: what's involved in the bench? like do you need our traces?
[03:33] Khalil: yes, sample traces and realistic distribution. we also need example prompts and success metrics per request (e.g., downstream QA pass, latency, token cost). we'll run both cold and warm-cache scenarios. typical checks: p50/p95 latency, throughput no-drop under sustained qps, CPU/GPU saturation, token cost.
[03:56] Priya: we care about 1) correctness (ROUGE-like for summaries), 2) latency under load, 3) cost per 1k tokens. success criteria will be a combination: automated QA >= 92% on gold set, P95 latency < 140ms during peak, and run-rate cost < $0.0015/token.
[04:22] Maya: ok, good set. we'll codify that into a KPI sheet. for the P95 target you mentioned (140ms), note earlier Mark said 120ms, so let's capture both: ideal <=120ms, acceptable <=140ms.
[04:37] Mark: acceptable band sounds fair. I want to call out cold-start for long conversations — there may be higher tail latencies; we will measure warm vs cold.
[04:48] Khalil: technical note on caching: if you have repeated prefixes (templated prompts) we can use prefix/K V cache to reduce tokens and latency; but that's workload dependent. also quantization: int8/4-bit will reduce memory footprint for dedicated but may affect quality — we'll include quality regression checks in the bench.
[05:10] Priya: our main decision hinge is: if Redwood hosted with VPC/KMS support can meet P95 and residency, we'd prefer hosted for speed. if not, dedicated reserved nodes. private on-prem only if dedicated can't meet residency or they require air-gapped controls.
[05:29] Ava: procurement question — what are the contract lengths for dedicated? and is there a trial reserved capacity?
[05:36] Maya: Dedicated typically has month-to-month reserved tiers for POC-sized commitments or 12-month discounted. We can propose a 3-month pilot reserved capacity option with break clauses.
[05:46] Devon: security — do you have SOC 2/ISO docs and evidence of HSM/KMS integration? and can we run a pen test?
[05:56] Lina: yes, we'll share the security pack. Redwood supports KMS integrations and we've done HSM flows with customers. pen tests are handled per contract; we can discuss scope.
[06:08] Chris: can you summarize the hybrid POC phases?
[06:12] Maya: phase 0: onboarding + integration tests on hosted dev endpoints (1 week). phase 1: functional validation on hosted, run unit QA (2 weeks). phase 2: performance bench on dedicated (1-2 weeks) — compare metrics; phase 3: decision and optional private deployment scaffolding. total 5-6 weeks if everything goes smoothly.
[06:36] Priya: that's acceptable. do you require synthetic traffic or live traffic?
[06:40] Khalil: start with anonymized historical traces; we can also run a shadow test in staging with low % of live traffic if you prefer. we will not keep raw PII and we'll follow your scrub rules.
[06:52] Mark: network egress concerns — for dedicated we need private peering and strict egress filters. is that supported?
[06:58] Maya: yes, dedicated supports VPC peering and egress controls. private supports complete customer control (on-prem or VPC private control plane).
[07:07] Devon: data at rest encryption — keys must be customer-owned for any stored context; can you guarantee that in hosted?
[07:14] Lina: hosted can be configured with customer KMS for stored artifacts in the dedicated/private tiers; for shared hosted (multi-tenant) some metadata may be redacted; we can walk through specifics in the security packet.
[07:28] Chris: timeline-wise we want bench results before our Q4 planning freeze. that's end of September ideally. is that realistic?
[07:36] Khalil: compressed bench and focused scope it's possible: if you supply traces by 9/19 we can run a 3-5 day stress and produce results by 9/26.
[07:45] Priya: ok so deliverable dates aligned.
[07:49] Maya: commercial note — cost delta between hosted and dedicated for your scale: hosted shared inference may be cheaper initially but at 650 qps peaks and 600 tokens, unit cost probably higher due to burst charges; dedicated amortizes GPU cost and gives predictable throughput. we'll include a modeled comparison in the pricing sheet.
[08:10] Chris: any competitors we should worry about? we've run small tests with Anthropic and OpenAI but cost was high; quality with Llama-family is good for our summarization.
[08:21] Khalil: we'll benchmark side-by-side as part of the POC if you want; we can run normalized latency/cost comparisons across model candidates. note though, cross-vendor bench has regulatory implications.
[08:35] Devon: we will need contractual clauses for data handling and an attestation for any third-party vendor testing.
[08:42] Maya: agreed. we'll add legal-friendly language and route it to Ava.
[08:48] Ava: perfect. procurement wants a short pilot MSA and a statement of work with clear exit terms.
[08:56] Maya: we'll propose a 3-month pilot MSA with a 2-week notice clause and a scoped SOW for bench and deliverables.
[09:04] Priya: on success criteria again — please capture the QA thresholds and also the regression tolerance for quality vs quantization. we cannot accept quality drop >2% relative to baseline.
[09:15] Khalil: noted. we'll include automatic regression tests: run the gold set with base FP16 and quantized variants; capture delta.
[09:24] Maya: ok let's recap next steps.
[09:26] Maya: Redwood to send: 1) sizing worksheet, 2) POC runbook + timeline, 3) security pack (SOC2/ISO/KMS details), 4) commercial pilot proposal with dedicated and hosted options. target send date 2025-09-15.
[09:44] Priya: Juno to send traces and acceptance criteria by 9/19.
[09:48] Maya: Khalil to schedule bench and prep harness; proposed week of 9/22.
[09:53] Chris: will loop in infra to provide traffic traces and a staging endpoint.
[09:58] Maya: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invites.
